article.title: Piece of cake
article.description: Meaning: something very easy to do. Example: 'Don't worry about the test, it'll be a piece of cake.' Register: informal. Similar idioms: 'a walk in the park', 'easy as pie'.
article.content: Meaning: something very easy to do. Example: 'Don't worry about the test, it'll be a piece of cake.' Register: informal. Similar idioms: 'a walk in the park', 'easy as pie'.

generated.caption:
Ever done something that felt incredibly easy? Then you know this idiom! 😉

"Piece of cake" is an informal way to say something is very easy to do.

For example: "Don't worry about the test, it'll be a **piece of cake**."

Save this idiom for when you need it! Share with a friend, and follow @EnglishVault for daily English lessons!
generated.script: Ye 'piece of cake' sunke aapko bhi lagta hai kya ki khaane ki baat ho rahi hai? Yaani cake ki? Actually, 'piece of cake' ka matlab hai ki koi cheez bahut easy hai, kuch mushkil nahi hai. Iska matlab hai 'something very easy to do'. Jaise agar koi aapko test ke liye bole, 'Don't worry about the test, it'll be a piece of cake.' Matlab test bahut easy hoga, tension mat lo. Ab samajh aaya? Next time jab koi cheez aapko bahut easy lage toh bolna 'It's a piece of cake!' Comment mein batao kya aapko ye pata tha ya aap bhi confuse hote the? slides.headlineRest: — What It Means When Something's So Easy!
slides.body: 'Piece of cake' is an informal idiom used to describe something that is extremely easy to do. It conveys that a task or situation requires minimal effort and presents no difficulty. For instance, you might reassure a friend by saying, 'Don't worry about the test, it'll be a piece of cake.' This phrase is often used in lighthearted conversations, much like other similar idioms such as 'a walk in the park' or 'easy as pie'.
